([[Bell Buckle, Tennessee]]) | college = [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] (2020–2021) | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2021) * 2× [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] (2018, 2019) }} '''Christopher Keon Johnson''' (born March 10, 2002) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]]. ==Early life and high school career== Two months before beginning high school, Johnson suffered [[open fracture]]s in four of his fingers, was thrown about 10 feet and lost consciousness in a [[fireworks]] accident. He underwent surgery to repair [[blood vessel]]s in his hand and avoid [[amputation]], and he underwent eight weeks of intensive [[physical therapy]].{{cite web |last1=Humphrey |first1=Nancy |title=Game On |url=https://hope.childrenshospitalvanderbilt.org/game-on/ |publisher=Vanderbilt Children's Hospital |accessdate=May 5, 2020 |date=June 10, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Kreager |first1=Tom |title=How top prospect Keon Johnson, wanted by UT Vols and others, almost ended his career before it began |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/02/13/nashville-high-school-basketball-ut-vols-keon-johnson-webb-school/2805130002/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |accessdate=May 5, 2020 |date=February 13, 2019}} Johnson played high school basketball for [[The Webb School (Bell Buckle, Tennessee)|The Webb School]] in [[Bell Buckle, Tennessee]]. In his sophomore season, he averaged 25.6 points, 10.2 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game, earning Division II-A [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball]] honors.{{cite web |title=2017-18 ALL-USA Tennessee Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-tennessee-boys-basketball-team |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=May 5, 2020 |date=April 16, 2018}} As a junior, Johnson averaged 25.3 points, 9.4 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game, leading his team to the Division II-A state semifinals. He repeated as Division II-A Tennessee Mr. Basketball.{{cite web |last1=Kreager |first1=Tom |title=Keon Johnson, Tennessee's top 2020 basketball prospect, plays with edge, even if that means technicals |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/01/tennessee-high-school-basketball-webb-star-keon-johnson-fouls-out-state-tssaa/3036815002/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |accessdate=May 5, 2020 |date=March 1, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Kreager |first1=Tom |title=James Wiseman, top college basketball prospect in country, wins first Mr. Basketball honor |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/05/tssaa-mr-and-miss-basketball-winners-announced/3052881002/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=March 5, 2019}} Early in his senior season, Johnson suffered a season-ending [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] injury. In four games, he averaged 30.5 points with 10.5 rebounds and 5.8 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Kreager |first1=Tom |title=Tennessee basketball signee Keon Johnson injures knee, expected back before postseason |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/12/17/tennessee-basketball-keon-johnson-injures-knee-out-six-weeks/2677356001/ |website=[[The Tennessean]] |accessdate=March 5, 2020 |date=December 17, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== On August 6, 2019, Johnson committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] over offers from [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], among others.{{cite web |title=Big in-state recruit Keon Johnson commits to Tennessee |url=https://www.wvlt.tv/content/news/Big-In-State-recruit-picks-Tennessee-524260141.html |publisher=[[WVLT-TV]] |accessdate=May 5, 2020 |date=August 6, 2019}} By the end of his high school career, Johnson was rated by major recruiting services as a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the highest ranked player in Tennessee in the 2020 class. He became the first top-ranked in-state prospect to commit to Tennessee since [[Robert Hubbs III]] in 2013.{{cite web |last1=Wilson |first1=Mike |title=Tennessee basketball signs three prominent recruits Wednesday |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2019/11/13/tennessee-vols-basketball-recruiting-jaden-springer-keon-johnson-rick-barnes/2556897001/ |website=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]] |accessdate=May 5, 2020 |date=November 13, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Keon Johnson | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Shelbyville, Tennessee|Shelbyville, TN]] | highschool = [[The Webb School (Bell Buckle, Tennessee)|The Webb School]] (TN) | feet = 6 | inches = 5 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = August 9, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 90 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = Tennessee 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 Tennessee Volunteers Recruiting Class | rivals school = tennessee | scout s = | espn schoolid = 2633 | 247 overall = 17 | rivals overall = 18 | espn overall = 28 | accessdate = August 18, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== On February 6, 2021, Johnson scored a career-high 27 points in an 82–71 win over [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite web |title=Johnson, Springer rally No. 11 Tennessee past Kentucky 82-71 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401258790 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=February 6, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 11.3 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game, and was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman Team. On April 7, 2021, Johnson declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Tennessee Vols' Keon Johnson to declare for NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31209073/tennessee-vols-keon-johnson-declare-nba-draft |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=April 7, 2021}} At the [[NBA Draft Combine]], he recorded the highest maximum [[vertical jump|vertical leap]] in combine history, at 48 inches.{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=Keon Johnson shatters combine record with historic max
